title: Learning decision trees from uniform random examples in polynomial time
formal: Is there a uniform randomized learner which, for all \(n,s\ge 1\) and rational \(\varepsilon \in (0,1)\), learns every size-at-most-s Boolean decision tree on n variables from uniform random labeled examples in time \(\operatorname{poly}(n,s,1/\varepsilon )\), with error at most \(\varepsilon\) and success probability at least \(2/3\)?
definitions: A decision tree has internal nodes querying one input coordinate, two outgoing edges labeled zero and one, and leaves labeled zero or one. Size counts all nodes. Samples are independent uniform \(x\in \{0,1\}^{n}\) labeled by the unknown target f. The learner receives \(n,s,\varepsilon\) and may draw samples but cannot request labels at chosen inputs. It outputs a Boolean circuit h of polynomial size, with \(\Pr_{x\text{ uniform}}[h(x)\ne f(x)]\le\varepsilon\) on at least two thirds of runs. All sampling, computation, circuit writing and evaluation costs use classical bit operations; the total worst-case learning time has one polynomial bound.

context_blocks.text: Decision trees are an elementary representation for Boolean classification. Uniform data removes distributional pathologies but still leaves open whether random examples suffice for fully polynomial learning.

Kalai and Teng contrast the unresolved uniform-distribution problem with their positive result for most perturbed product distributions. Chosen-input queries can provide information unavailable from examples alone. The existing proper-learning card allows membership queries and requires a tree output. This target permits improper output but removes that query access.

context_blocks.title: Additional source and scope
context_blocks.text: The backdoor-defense source also raises efficient learning of polynomial-size decision trees from uniform random labeled examples. The access is random examples; free membership queries at selected inputs would change the learning problem.

why: Settle the sample-only computational learnability of a canonical interpretable Boolean model.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
